programme: No single recognizable module emerges. The factors fall into unrelated functional classes with no shared complex, pathway, or upstream/downstream relationship documented among them: PIAS2 (SUMO E3 ligase, alpha-synuclein/IFN-beta axis), SATB2 (chromatin matrix-attachment TF), MYCN (neural-crest oncogene network), HDAC3 (histone deacetylase), DACH1/SKIL (Wnt- and TGF-beta-pathway repressors), FOXJ1 (motile-cilia master regulator), FOXF1 (mesenchymal/vascular TF), THRA (thyroid hormone receptor), ARX (pancreatic islet/forebrain homeobox TF), PLAG1 (IGF2-driven salivary-gland oncogene), ATOH8 (hepcidin/iron-axis bHLH TF). These are drawn from at least six distinct developmental and signaling contexts (ciliogenesis, Wnt/TGF-beta repression, thyroid hormone response, pancreatic/neural patterning, iron homeostasis, proteostasis) with no reported physical or genetic interaction linking them.
role_in_a: Not established from this record. Only DACH1 has direct literature placing it in Head_and_Neck_Cancer specifically (Wnt-pathway silencing by promoter methylation in oral/oropharyngeal tumors, PMID 25487617); MYCN has an Open Targets association (percentile 0.8268) and partial ReMap binding evidence but no HNC-specific literature confirmation; SKIL has only generic-cancer evidence, not HNC-specific.
role_in_b: Not established as a joint programme. PIAS2 and SATB2 each have individual literature placing them in Parkinsons_Disease (PIAS2 via IFN-beta blockade and alpha-synuclein SUMOylation, PMIDs 34234281/29180403; SATB2 via disease progression, PMID 31539139), but nothing connects PIAS2 and SATB2 to each other mechanistically, and the remaining factors (MYCN, HDAC3, ARX, FOXJ1, etc.) have only Open Targets percentile signals or no PD evidence at all.
shared_axis: No mechanism ties these factors together across the two diseases. The recurrence pattern looks like independent, tissue/context-specific developmental or oncogenic regulators being detected in their respective disease's network rather than a shared axis linking Head_and_Neck_Cancer to Parkinsons_Disease.
reasoning: The twelve factors span at least six unrelated biological domains with no documented complex or pathway connecting more than one or two of them at a time, and the per-factor literature is almost entirely single-disease (PIAS2/SATB2 in PD only, DACH1 in HNC only) or absent/uncertain for the rest. Forcing a module here would mean naming a story that isn't in the factors; twelve co-occurring TFs are not by themselves a mechanism.
support: PMID 34234281 — PIAS2 blocks IFN-beta signaling, proposed basis for PD dementia (PD only, no HNC link). PMID 29180403 — SUMOylation/ubiquitination (PIAS2-relevant) regulate alpha-synuclein aggregation in PD (PD only). PMID 31539139 — SATB2 (with dysbindin-1) implicated in PD progression (PD only). PMID 25487617 — DACH1 (with DKK1, WIF1) silenced by methylation in oral/oropharyngeal cancer, i.e. HNC (HNC only). PMID 23764425 — SKIL as a cancer driver at 3q26, but not HNC-specific and not disease-pairing evidence.
how_to_falsify: Test whether any two of these factors physically or genetically interact in a shared pathway in matched tissue — e.g., co-immunoprecipitation or ChIP-seq for PIAS2 and SATB2 in Parkinson's-affected neurons, or MYCN ChIP-seq in HNC tumor tissue at PRKN/PD-relevant loci — and check whether any single factor (most plausibly MYCN, which has Open Targets signal in both diseases) shows regulatory activity at a documented target in both HNC and PD tissue; finding such a shared node would overturn the incoherent call.
caveats: The 414 patient-group comparisons are drawn from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance counts (e.g. PIAS2 282/414) reflect repeated sub-grouping of the same underlying cohorts rather than 414 independent replications — treat the fractions as far less powerful than they look. Tissue pairing is blood (PD) vs head_neck (HNC), two anatomically and functionally unrelated tissues, which raises the bar for any claimed shared mechanism. The tissue-generic exclusion list (AR, TWIST1, SMAD3, RUNX2, CEBPB, etc.) removed several factors that might otherwise have suggested a stromal/immune story, and the single-view exclusions (HOXA11, BCL11B, CREB1, GATA2, etc.) rule out any account built on one patient subgroup — neither exclusion list points toward an alternative coherent module among the surviving factors.
